chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir who said:

Abu al-Ward asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was with him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are upon me like the back of my mother' one hundred times. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He is able to free one slave for each time.' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then is he able to feed sixty poor people one hundred times?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then is he able to fast for two consecutive months one hundred times?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'He should distribute [the expiations] among them.'

key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: Like the back of my mother (formula for Zihar)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for repeating Zihar multiple times in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that repeated *Zihar* declarations require cumulative expiation rather than a single penalty, emphasizing the financial and physical burden on the husband. The Imam employs a dialectical method, asking the companion Abu al-Ward about his capacity for freeing slaves, feeding the poor, or fasting, to determine the appropriate level of expiation for each instance. This ruling underscores the principle that *Zihar* is a serious marital disruption requiring proportional restitution based on individual ability.
